title: What Longevity Economics Is
definition: Longevity Economics: economics of much longer lives.
description:
Longevity Economics — Signature Edition: economics of much longer lives. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature economics hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: life-course models rethought, economics logistics rebuilt, pension redesign reimagined for the century ahead. This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the career arcs ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Longevity Economics
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Longevity Economics.
description:
The Signature vision of Longevity Economics does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature economics hulls program, charter one: master life-course models at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale economics logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate pension redesign systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Longevity Economics becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

t: 2030 — First city-scale economics hulls pilots launch: life-course mode
title: 2030 — First city-scale economics hulls pilots launch: life-course mode
definition: 2030 milestone on the Longevity Economics roadmap.
description:
First city-scale economics hulls pilots launch: life-course models issuance and economics logistics exchange running live.

What must be true first: the life-course models results have to replicate outside the lab, economics logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and pension redesign operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed life-course models demonstrations, economics logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting pension redesign uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Longevity Economics
definition: Estimates Longevity Economics readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Longevity Economics components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a economics hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Longevity Economics Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Longevity Economics operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Longevity Economics installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 4540 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where life-course models monitoring, economics logistics redundancy, or pension redesign maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Longevity Economics Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Longevity Economics: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Longevity Economics — economics of much longer lives.

Phase 1 — Prove (life-course models): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (economics logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (pension redesign): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (career arcs): economics hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and society-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
